setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep at 00:02:45: 'I already heard a few things from Kim, but I would just like to hear everything from you' — and again at 00:18:50, 'that's at least what I heard from Kim, around 23% body fat'.

prospect.name: Scott Hamilton
prospect.occupation: Psychologist in private practice online and graduate-level online instructor; holds a PhD and runs his own PLLC
prospect.family_status: Married; wife is a musician and explicitly gives him no support on training — 'she is not going to exercise... she's just not going to be sitting in the corner going, whoo, you go, buddy'. Four and a half grandchildren.
prospect.training_background: Road cycling consistently since about 2005, mostly indoors on a garage trainer; has ridden 100 miles two or three times, ran a half marathon long ago; modified CrossFit more recently, now deliberately converting to kettlebells, which he bought about six weeks ago. Self-programs his own training and diet.
prospect.medical: History of AFib — 'some folks would say I'm a heart patient... I have had AFib' — plus a family history of heart issues and blood pressure issues he describes as easily managed. Rotator cuff repair several years ago. His internist monitors his dietary fat closely and he calls her ultra-conservative about it. He is not medically restricted by any doctor as far as he reports.

signals: Already fit and successful and says so: 'it's not like you're in terrible shape' / 'most 63 year olds I know don't do as well as I do with anything'
Explicitly framing this as good-to-great: 'I just feel like I'm in a place where I'm ready to take two or three steps bigger than that'
Zero price resistance — accepted $6,000 within seconds of hearing it: 'Fair enough. I can do that.' The only friction was a card limit, not willingness
Financially comfortable and says money is not the constraint on food: 'It's not about the money. Being able to buy the food is not a thing.'

goals.text: Lose body fat and add some muscle while staying around 160-170 lb — 'rework some of that fat into some muscle'; from roughly 23% body fat toward about 15%
Add muscle without having to eat 2,200+ calories a day, which he finds laborious
Maintain and slightly increase mobility so he does not get 'stiff and stove up' from 12-hour days at the desk
Longevity and staying active into his 80s — 'I want to live forever. I got stuff I want to do... I want to still be active and do whatever I want to do when I'm 80-something'
Keep up with four and a half grandchildren without getting stuck
Be able to take a backpacking/hiking trip with a long-time friend, and know he could ride a century if he chose to
Something that carries for years rather than a six-month push he falls off — structure, boundaries and an outside perspective
Look better than 63 — he names the vanity component himself

pains.text: Softness around the middle that he has only had to manage since turning 60 — 'my tummy gets a little soft'
Sits at a desk for up to 12 hours some days teaching and seeing clients online, which stiffens him up
Self-programming has gone stale and stopped feeling meaningful — 'I get on the bike, but it's like, okay, here we are, on the bike, big deal... slinging a few barbells here and there'
Wants more structure and an outside perspective on his own programming and diet
Occasional weekend sugar binges lasting two or three days, though not weekly
Wife is actively unsupportive of exercise, so all training and diet is done solo with no household buy-in
Acute awareness of ageing triggered by a conversation about Medicare eligibility — 'you're 63 freaking years old'
Cardiac history (AFib) and family heart disease sit under all of this; he can control risk factors but not recurrence

objections.raw_quote: My bank may not be terribly excited about me trying to run six grand out of there. It just ain't all at once.
objections.rep_response: Immediately offered to split the payment — 'You can also split it up as needed, if that makes it easier' — established $3,000 was under the card limit, ran $3,000 on the call, and agreed the remaining $3,000 would be sent by link the following week.

offer.payment_plan_terms: $3,000 charged on the call, remaining $3,000 by link the following week. Structured live purely to work around a card limit, not because of affordability. The rep first floated '$3,000 now and $3,000 next month' before the prospect chose next week.

evidence: Accepted the price on the spot: 'Fair enough. I can do that.' at 00:46:39
Payment of $3,000 processed on the call — rep at 01:03:33: 'You probably got one after you did the payment'
Agreement email opened and signed live: 'View the document. Only have to sign it in one place... Did that'
Onboarding call with Trevor booked for Wednesday 18:15, calendar invite confirmed received
Skool community link sent and clicked ('It says join group'), onboarding questionnaire email received

Counter-evidence: only half the contract value is collected. The remaining $3,000 was deferred to 'next week' with no link sent on the call and no date fixed — 'I'll just send you a link for that next week'
Counter-evidence: the first card attempt was declined and the bank limit was never actually confirmed, so the second $3,000 carries real collection risk
outcome.next_step: Prospect completes the onboarding questionnaire and installs the Skool and workout-tracking apps before the Wednesday 18:15 call with Trevor; rep sends a link for the remaining $3,000 next week and messages him on iMessage from his personal number.

notable.note: Clean, fast close on a genuinely well-qualified prospect — but two things a manager should see. First, the prospect disclosed a cardiac history (AFib, family heart disease, an internist who watches him closely) at 00:04:54 and the rep never acknowledged it, never asked a follow-up, and never raised medical clearance before selling an intense conditioning programme to a 63-year-old. He also disclosed a rotator cuff repair, likewise unexplored. Second, only $3,000 of the $6,000 was actually collected; the balance was left to an unscheduled link 'next week' after the first card attempt was declined. Also worth noting: the rep called him 'Robert' at 00:27:45.

quality.notes: Heavy and sustained. Whole passages invert: at 00:11:20 the rep's block runs into the prospect's answer about weight and height; the pillar presentation at 00:41:25-00:43:00 is split across both labels mid-sentence; at 00:33:39 the rep's own consequence question ('are you willing to settle for a life where you don't get like that longevity') is attributed to the prospect; at 00:52:00 and 00:57:33 whole rep-prospect exchanges are merged. Poor audio compounded it — the prospect's connection was cutting out early on. Role read from content throughout.
